chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

"A man should not wash the garment in which he enters the state of Ihram until he exits it, even if it becomes dirty, unless he becomes Junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) or something else happens, in which case he washes it."
And there is no harm in wearing the marked garments, but avoiding them is superior.

key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: enters the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim wash their Ihram garment during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of Ihram garments, emphasizing that minor soiling does not necessitate washing, thereby preserving the garment's continuity until the pilgrim exits the state of Ihram or encounters major impurity (Janabah). The distinction regarding 'marked' garments reflects the scholarly preference (Istihbab) for simplicity and avoiding distinctive clothing that might imply status, aligning with the spiritual humility of the pilgrimage. This ruling underscores the balance between ritual purity and the practical realities of travel in Shia jurisprudence.
